  SUBJECT:  ORDINANCE NO, 582
  AMENDING Tl-IE HAWAIIAN GARDENS MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADD
  CHAPTER 9.30, RELATING TO LOUD OR UNRULY PARTIES

  Rl;COMMEr,JQATION
  Staff reoommends that the City Council introduce for first reading:

  Ordin.ance No, 582:AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF HAWAIIAN GARDENS,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE HAWAIIAN GARDl::NS MUNICIPAL CODE  ro
  ADD CHAF-iTER 9,30, RELATING TO LOUD OR UNRULY PARTIES

  !;IACKGROUND
  While the City currently has a noise ordinance In effect that addresses certain types of
  Increased noise levels in residential areas, the ordinance does not always dlrectly
  address Impacts. resulting from loud and boisterous parties. Such loud or unruly
  gatherings can constltuta a threat to the peace, hea!lh, safety, or general welfare of the
  public _as a result of, among other things, excessive noise, excessive traffic, obstruction
  of public streets, public drunkenness, the service of alcohol to minors, fights,
  disturbances of the peace, and lrttering. As a result, such parties are a burden on City
  resources, as the City and/or law enforcement are often required to respond to
  complaints about such loud or unruly gatherings in order to restore the peaoe and
  protect public safety.

  At the April 23, 2019 City Council meeting, Iha City Council directed Slaff lo amend the
  Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code to(1) discourage and deter the occurrence of loud or
  unruly conduct and gatherings, and (2) strengthen the City's ability to regulate and
  abate the sama.lri response, Staff hereby Introduces to the City Council Ordinance No.
  682, which adds a chapter to the Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code relating to loud or
  unruly parties and conduot, in an effort to provide the City an additional enforcement·
  mechanism to address such gatherings and conduct.

  Pursuant to Government ·code sections 36934 and 36937, ordinances are "introduced"
  at a City Council meeting, "passed" (i.e., approved) at a later City Council meeting, and
  then taka effect 30 days after passage.

616119
   P,60
  DISCUSSION
  Ordinance No. 582 seeks, by adding Chapter 9.30 to the Municipal Code, to regulate
  "loud or unruly conduct" to (1) discourage and deter the occurrence cif loud or unruly
  conduct and gatherings and (2) strengthen the City's ability to regulate and abate this
  conduct.The proposed Chapter 9.30 would prohibit, among other things, an individual
  from knowingly holding, permitting, or facilitatlng any party at which there is loud or
  unruly conduct, or conduct that otherwise disturbs the quiet enjoyment of private or
  public property.

  The proposed Chapter 9.30 exceeds the scope of the existing Chapter 9.29, Noise
  Control, of the City's Municipal Code. For example, Chapter 9.30 would:

  1. Allow the City to regulate, enforce, and abate disruptive, excessive, or intrusive
  noise in circumstances where the noise standards set forth in Chapter 9.29 may·
  be more difficult to apply.

  2. Prohibit a loud or unruly gathering at any point in the day if such a gathering
  results in loud, excessive, or Intrusive noise, even without the City's enforcement
  officer having access to a decibel reader, because the proposed
  ordinanceprovides alternative criteria to serve as a basis for enforcement. (By
  comparison, the Noise Control ordinancerequires theCity enforcement officers to
  measure the noise emanating from the gathering,with a decibel reader,to
  establish the noise standards set forth in Chapter 29 exceed the thresholds
  established In that ordinance.

  3. Regulate not only noise, but also other loud or unruly conduct associated with
  disruptive parties, such as obstruction of public streets, illegal parking of cars,
  fighting, illegal conduct, or other conduct that could constitute a threat to the
  peace, health, safety, or general welfare of the public.

  4. Provide that a person who violates any provision of the proposed ordinance
  would be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by (i) a fine not to exceed five
  hundred dollars ($500), (ll) imprisonment In a city jail or in the county jail, as the
  committing magistrate may direct, for a period not to exceed ninety days, or (iii)
  by both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court.

  5. Provide for a procedure by which the City may recover costs it Incurs in
  response to a loud or unruly gathering at a premises where such gathering
  occurs within 180 days of a previous response by a city enforcement officer to a
  loud or unruly gathering at that same premises. These costs could be recovered
  from the party's host, guests present at the party, the premises' residents, and in
  the case of any of the foregoing who are minors, the parents and/or guardians of
  such minors.

  FISCAL IMPACT
  There is no adverse fiscal Impact to the City associated with this action. The adoption
  of the Ordinance could result, however, in the City recovering costs associated with
  abating loud or unruly conduct.

832657.1

  ALTERNATIVES
  The City Council could decide not to adopt the proposed unruly gathering ordinance and
  continue to address violations through the existing noise ordinance only. This alternative
  will continue to limit the ability of the Sheriff and staff to address unruly gatherings, and
  recover certain costs associated with such unruly gatherings.

  CEQA ANALYSIS
  This Ordinance is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (Public
  Resources Code, § 21000, et seq; "CEQA"). The adoption of the proposed ordinance is
  not a "project" underCEQA and the State CEQA Guidelines (14 Cal. Code of
  Regulations, § 15000, et seq.) as it does not have the 'potential for resulting in either a
  direct physical change in the environment, or a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical
  change In the environment." (CEQA Guidelines, §§ 15060(c)(2)-(3), 15378(a).)
  Moreover, even if the Ordinance qualified as a project under CEQA, the Ordinance is
  exempt from CEQA as "It can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the
  activtty in question may have a significant effect on the environment." (State CEQA
  Guidelines,§ 15061(b)(3).)

  In particular, the Ordinance will not result in any construction, has no growth-inducing
  impacts, and will not result in any direct or indirect physical change in the environment.
  To the contrary, the Ordinance allows the City to promote the peace, health, safety, and
  general welfare of the public by prohibitl.ng loud or unruly conduct and gatherings in the
  City.

  CITY OF HAWAIIAN GARDENS
  ORDINANCE NO. 682

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF HAWAIIAN GARDENS, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE
  HAWAIIAN GARDENS MUNICIPAL CODE· TO ADD
  CHAPTER 9.30, RELATING TO LOUD OR UNRULY
  PARTIES

  WHEREAS, the City of Hawaiian Gardens is authorized by Article 11, section 7
of the California Constitution to make and enforce within its limits all local, police,
sanitary, and other ordinances and regulations not in conflict with general laws; and

  WHEREAS, the City is further authorized by Government Code section 36901 to
Impose fines, penalties, and forfeitures for violations of the City's ordinances; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council finds and determines that parties, gatherings or.
events on private property can constitute a threat to the peace, health, safety or general
welfare of the public; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council. further finds and determines that City enforcement
officers have been required to make many return calls to parties, gatherings or events in
order to disperse uncooperative and unruly participants, and such return calls drain the
personnel power and resources of the City's law enforcement officers and can leave
other areas of the City without minimal levels of law enforcement protection so as to
create a significant hazard. to the safety of citizens and police officers; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Hawaiian Gardens desires to amend Title 9 of the
Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code by adding Chapter 9.30 to regulate loud and unruly
parties and to ensure the safety of its citizens and law enforcement officers; and

  WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Ordinance have
occurred.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF HAWAIIAN
GARDENS DOES ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The City Council hereby finds and determines that the Recitals above
are true and correct and are incorporated herein.

  Section 2. Chapter 9.30 of Title 9 of the Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code is
hereby added in its entirety to read as follows:

  Title 9 - PUBLIC PEACE, MORALS AND WELFARE

  Chapter 9.30- LOUD OR UNRULY PARTIES

9.30.010  Declaration of findings and policy.

66320,00001\32049174.2
   P,63
  I! is hereby found and declared that

  A.  Some gatherings of people become loud or unruly to the point that they
  constitute a threat to the peace, health, safety, or general welfare of the
  public as a result of, among other things, excessive noise, excessive
  traffic, obstruction of public streets, public drunkenness, the service of
  alcohol lo minors, fights, disturbances of the peace, and littering.

  B.  The City is often required to respond to complaints about such loud or
  unruly gatherings in order lo restore the peace and protect public safety.
  These loud or unruly gatherings are thus a burden on scarce city
  resources.

  C.  In order to discourage and deter the occurrence of loud or unruly
  gatherings, the City seeks to further regulate these gatherings as forth in
  this Chapter.

9.30.020  Definitions.

  The following terms as used in this Chapter shall be defined herein as follows:

  A.  "Alcohol" shall have the meaning set forth In Business and Professions
  Code section 23003.

  B.  "Alcoholic beverage" shall have the meaning set forth in Business and
  Professions Code section 23004.

  C.  "City enforcement officer'' means any authorized employee or designee of
  the chief of police, Los Angeles county sheriff's department, or community
  development director.

  D.  "Host" Is hereby defined to include (i) a person who owns, rents, leases, or
  otherwise has control of the premises where the party occurs; and/or
  (ii) any person who organizes, supervises, sponsors, or is otherwise
  responsible for a party;

  E.  "Loud or unruly conduct" is hereby defined lo include, without limitation,
  the following:

  1.  Conduct or activity at a premises, by itsetf or cumulatively with
  other conduct or activity at the premises, that results in noise levels
  exceeding the noise standards set forth in this Code and in
  particular the standards set forth in Sections 9.29.060, 9.29.070,
  9.29.080, 9.29.090, and/or 9.29.120;

  2.  Conduct or activity at a premises, by itself or cumulatively with
  other conduct or activity at the premises, that results in loud,
  excessive, impulsive, or intrusive sound or noise that would annoy
  or disturb persons of ordinary sensibilities, even if such noise does
  not exceed the standards set forth in Sections 9.29.060, 9.29.070,

  9.29.080, 9.29.090, and/or 9.29.120. The factors, standards, and
  conditions that may be considered in determining whether conduct
  or activity results In such sound or noise include, but are not limited
  to, the following:

  (a)  The level of the noise;

  (b)  The level and intensity of the background (ambient) noise, if
  any;

  (c)  The proximity of the noise to residential or commercial
  sleeping areas;

  (d)  The nature, density, and zoning of the area within which the
  noise emanates;

  (e)  The density of inhabitation of the area within which the noise

  (f)  The time of day or night that the noise occurs;

  (g)  The duration of the noise;

  (h)  The nature and character of the noise (e.g., whether the

  (i)  Whether the nature of the noise is natural or unnatural;

  (j)  Whether the noise is constant, recurrent, or intermittent; and

  {k)  Whether the noise is produced by a commercial or
  noncommercial activity.

  3.  Obstruction of public streets (e.g., by crowds or vehicles);

  4.  Illegal parking of cars, such as the parking of a car on a lawn or the
  parking of a car in such manner as to block a driveway.

  5.  Public drunkenness or public urination.

  6.  Fighting, including assaults and batteries.

  7.  Vandalism or littering.

  8.  Underage drinking or the service of alcohol to minors.

  9.  Illegal conduct.

  10.  Conduct that results in a complaint to a city enforcement officer,
  provided that the city enforcement officerdetermines that such
  conduct would be offensive to reasonable persons of normal

  sensitivities situated similarly to persons inhabiting adjacent or
  surrounding properties or that such conduct otherwise constitutes
  loud or unruly conduct.

  11.  Other conduct that could constitute a threat to the peace, health,
  safety, or general welfare of the public.

  F.  "Loud or unruly gathering" means a party at which there is loud or unruly
  conduct.

  G.  "Minor" means any person less than twenty-one (21) years of age.

  H.  "Party" means a gathering of persons at a residence or on other private
  property or public property.

  I.  "Premises" means the private property (including any yard or driveway)

  J.  "Response" means and refers to any action taken by the City and/or a city
  enforcement officertaken to address, abate, confront, investigate,
  intervene in, or otherwise respond to loud or unruly conduct at a party,
  including but not limited to any instance in which a city enforcement officer
  entersor steps onto a premises at which the city enforcement officer has
  reason to believe that loud or unruly conduct is occurring or has just
  recently occurred.

  K.  "Subsequent response" means and refers to any response by the City
  and/or a city enforcement officerto a loud or unruly gathering at a
  premises, where such gathering occurs within 180 days of a previous
  response by the City and/or city enforcement officerto a loud or unruly
  gathering at that same premises.

  L.  "Underage drinking" means consumption of alcohol or an alcoholic
  beverage by a minor.

9.30.030  Prohibited gatherings.

  A.  It shall be unlawfulto knowingly hold, permit, or facilitateany party at which
  there is loud or unruly conduct, or conduct that otherwise disturbs the
  quiet enjoyment of private or public property.

  B.  For purposes of this section, a person knowingly holds, permits, facilitates,
  or participates in a party at which there is loud or unruly conduct when the
  person is aware or should reasonably have been aware of such conduct
  occurring at the party.

  C.  A host shall be presumed to have known or should have known of loud or
  unruly conduct at a party if the host is present on the premises at any
  point during the party or notice has been issued as set forth in Section
  9.39.060 of this Code.

  D.  A host need not be present at the premises to be liable for a violation of
  this chapter. If the host is a minor and the premises Is owned, rented or
  leased by the host's parents or guardians, the parents or guardians may
  be held jointly and severally liable for violations of this chapter.
  E.  It is unlawful for any person to engage in loud or unruly conduct, or to
  attend and participate in a loud or unruly gathering.
9.30.040  Noise restriction - Bands, amplification, etc.

  It shall be unlawful to hold, permit, facilitate, or participate in any party in which a
band, orchestra, radio, phonograph, stereo, sound system, or other sound reproduction
and/or amplification device or system produces loud and unreasonable sound at any
point between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., if such noise is sufficiently loud
an.d unreasonable in volume level, duration, and character so as to disturb the comfort,
health, peace, safety, or repose of reasonable persons of ordinary sensibilities in the
surrounding area.

9.30.050  Penalty for violation - Fines and confinement.

  A.  Any person who violates any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a
  misdemeanor punishable by (i) a fine not to exceed five hundred dollars
  ($500), (ii) imprisonment in a city jail or in the county jail, as the
  committing magistrate may direct, for a period not to exceed ninety days,
  or (iii) by both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court.

  B.  Each violation shall constitute a separate offense and shall be punishable
  as such.
